activities.name: compEpicsMatch

config.prompt: The shared deep archive — pair each epic with its question and technology:

pairs.right: what a mortal should do with death — the flood tablet George Smith read aloud in 1872, comparative literature's founding sensation
what honour is worth — Parry's oral-formulaic machinery, a technique for composing without writing
dharma — duty in impossible situations, roughly ten times the Iliad and Odyssey combined, the Bhagavad Gita at its centre
performed by jeliw, never fixed, its charter of social roles recited for seven centuries

config.why: Same questions — mortality, duty, glory, founding — different technologies of transmission: comparison begins here.

activities.anchor: each singing is a new realisation of a tradition
activities.caption: find the line the formulas refute
activities.name: compHomerSpot

config.prompt: One line of this Homeric authorship report is wrong — click it:
lines: Parry's 1930s fieldwork showed the repeated phrases are oral-formulaic machinery.
Every performance is a new making, not a recitation of a fixed text.
The written Iliad is one crystallisation of a performance practice centuries older.
Homer's identity is settled: one literate poet wrote both epics down.
The authorship question became a researchable comparative problem.
config.correction: 'Homer' may name a singular genius, a cumulative tradition, or both — the oral-formulaic finding is what made it researchable.
config.why: Lord confirmed the machinery in living oral epics — composition without writing.

items.label: Tolstoy describing property as 'sparking and hiving off' — ownership strange again

activities.caption: drag the divider — reaction versus condition
activities.name: compBreaksCompare

config.prompt: The two great breaks, comparatively — drag the divider:

before.label: Modernism — a worldwide reaction
before.text: Mechanised war, urban speed, collapsed certainties; the echoes run from Lagos to Tokyo — Ulysses compresses Homer's epic day into Dublin's ordinary one.

after.label: Postmodernism — a condition of global media
after.text: Borges's infinite library, Pynchon's paranoid systems, metafiction confessing its own fictionality; grand narratives lose credit (Lyotard's definition).

config.why: Both breaks are arguments about what representation can do after disaster.

activities.anchor: Reading modernism as a European crisis misplaces half the archive
activities.caption: true or false — the break was polycentric
activities.name: compPolyJudge

statements.s: São Paulo's Modern Art Week (1922) launched a Brazilian programme culminating in Macunaíma — a 'hero with no character' assembled from Amerindian myth and urban slang.
statements.why: The break's techniques are portable; its causes are local.

statements.s: The negritude poets built a modernist French against the empire that owned the language.
statements.why: Césaire and Senghor, Paris in the 1930s.

statements.s: Each modernism answers the same collapsed certainty.
statements.why: The causes are local — each answers a different collapsed certainty.

statements.s: Translation carried the toolkit faster than the metropolitan centres noticed.
statements.why: Kawabata's New Sensationists, the Harlem Renaissance inside English — the experiment was polycentric from the start.

activities.anchor: Translation's history is also the history of languages being made
activities.caption: pair each translation event with the language it made
activities.name: compBibleMatch

config.prompt: Translations that made languages — pair the event with its deposit:

pairs.right: fixed vernacular German prose style for centuries
some 80% of the King James New Testament is Tyndale
the first grammars of hundreds of languages — documentation and imposition in one parcel
created modern Japanese prose — the receiving language as active party

config.why: Translation flows downhill in prestige less often than it flows from power — and every translation deposits a layer in the borrower's literature.

activities.anchor: Scripture translation remains the world's biggest literary project
activities.caption: call the count — Bibles in languages
activities.name: compScriptureEstimate

config.prompt: By the Wycliffe Global Alliance's 2024 count, the complete Bible exists in how many languages?
config.why: 756 — with New Testaments in about 1,800 and work under way in more than 3,200, against roughly 7,000 living languages: thousands still waiting. Every translation creates a literary tradition — hymnody, proverb collections, orthographies, the first printed book in hundreds of languages.
config.context: The book trade's inverse: the biggest seller is the least traded across languages.

activities.anchor: which is why comparative literature leans on its craft neighbour
activities.caption: find the line the editions contradict
activities.name: compTextSpot

config.prompt: One line of this textual report is wrong — click it:
lines: Gilgamesh is edited from fragmentary tablets across a millennium of copies.
The Mahabharata's Critical Edition collated over a thousand manuscripts (Pune, 1919–1966).
The Venetus A of ~1000 CE is the Iliad's most famous manuscript; the Alexandrians were history's first textual critics.
Sundiata exists in a definitive printed text.
A scholarly edition is an argument about which variants deserve the name of the work.
config.correction: Sundiata has no text at all in the classical sense — its 'editions' are transcriptions of performances, each one already an interpretation.
config.why: Reading world literature knowingly means reading the edition's apparatus as part of the text.
